history.summary: A 1,561 sqft 3BR/2-bath at The Centris asking $1.99M ($1,275 psf) — the algo's 844 and its 88 valuation score both rest on a 'discount' that is not a discount. The Centris trades in two hard PSF tiers: mainstream stock on floors 06-15 cleared a $1,634-1,640 psf median across 35 URA prints in the last 24 months, while ground-floor PES (floors 01-05: $1,277/$1,251/$801) and top-floor void/loft units (floors 16-20: $1,278/$1,175) clear around $1,225-1,275. The ask lands exactly on that lower tier's median, not below it, and the 3BR-with-only-2-baths configuration (780 sqft per bathroom, versus 3 baths on every mainstream 1,238-1,572 sqft unit currently listed) marks it as one of those compromised formats. You are paying a fair price for the project's least liquid product.
history.rating_rationale: Not an Avoid and nowhere near a Buy. The price is fair for what the unit is, the project's fundamentals are genuinely strong (Boon Lay MRT lobby-to-platform, 79yr lease, OCR, 610 units, 50+ deals/yr, 97.7% of resales profitable on 603 matched pairs), and the downside looks contained. But every point of apparent edge is a format artifact. The two largest MMR contributors — age_value +11.98 and psf_value +6.34, roughly 18 of the ~26 net points above base — are generated by a -15% to -16% gap to the district/size-band median that is really the -22% floor/format tier discount this project has always applied. The control case is decisive: a 1,528 sqft unit on floors 11-15 transacted at $1,562 psf in May-25, and a 1,292 sqft unit on floor 01-05 transacted at $1,277 psf in Oct-25 while identical 1,292 sqft units upstairs fetched $1,587-1,633. Size does not create this gap; floor and format do. The v3.8 low-floor defence never engaged here (low_floor component = 0.00) because the listing carries no floor data and The Centris has no stack profile, so the artifact passed straight through into the score. Carry is thin on top of that: the scorer's $6,025 rent is a project-wide 3BR average applied to a unit whose strata area is padded with non-liveable space — realsmart's actual 3BR median is $5,300 across 72 contracts, which puts real gross yield near 3.2% and net near 1.8%. And for the same $1.99M you can buy the mainstream, three-bath, high-floor stock in this very project (1,066 sqft at $1.81M, 1,259 sqft at $2.06M) that carries the liquidity the 844 score is implicitly crediting to this unit.
red_flags: No discount exists. The $1,275 psf ask sits at the median of The Centris's compromised-format tier (floors 01-05: $1,251 median; floors 16-20: $1,226 median, last 24mo), not below it. The -16% vs age-adjusted district median is a permanent structural level, not a dislocation.

3BR with only 2 baths at 1,561 sqft (780 sqft/bath). Every mainstream Centris unit listed at 1,238-1,572 sqft carries 3 baths, including the 1,572 sqft comparison listing 500108309 at $1,399 psf. The bathroom count is the tell that a large share of the strata area is PES patio or void, not liveable space.

Score artifact: age_value +11.98 and psf_value +6.34 dominate the 844 and both derive from the phantom discount. The low_floor damper reads 0.00 because no floor data was scraped and no stack profile exists, so the v3.8 defence built for exactly this case did not fire. Valuation 88 is contaminated the same way.

Exit liquidity is the real risk. Across 108 URA prints spanning 20 years only ~10 are 1,500+ sqft. The project's 'deep buyer pool' and 50+ deals/yr belong to the 872-1,442 sqft stock; this format clears only at deep PSF concessions (Mar-25: 2,347 sqft at $801 psf, in a hot market).

Weak carry. realsmart's 3BR median rent is $5,300 (72 contracts, latest 12 ranging $4,700-6,800); rent tracks liveable area, not padded strata area. On $1.99M that is ~3.2% gross / ~1.8% net, below the scorer's assumed 3.63%.

Resident-reported environmental negatives that hit a low-floor unit hardest: low-flying aircraft noise, industrial odours (burning rubber, cocoa from nearby factories), heavy traffic noise from the Boon Lay bus interchange below, and no guest parking. realsmart's own copy calls the surroundings 'quite busy'.

Trailing appreciation is a size-mix artifact. The 6.87% ura_5yr_cagr is inflated because 2021-22 prints were penthouse/PES-heavy ($833-977 psf) while 2025-26 prints are mainstream 900-1,300 sqft at $1,600-1,700. Do not read it as a forward rate.
17 years old, entering the 15-20yr segment where the measured age-PSF decay re-accelerates to ~2.6%/yr.
JLD's July-2026 white site (up to 1,200 private units) and the wider masterplan are competing supply inside a 5-7yr exit window, not only a demand catalyst.
catalysts: Best-in-class connectivity: Boon Lay MRT (EW27/JS8) at 59-110m with direct lift access, integrated with Jurong Point mall and Boon Lay bus interchange. MRT proximity is one of the few forward signals that survives clustering.
OCR region — the strongest realized forward segment in the backtest (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).

Exceptional project-level downside record: 589 profitable vs 14 unprofitable resales (97.7% on 603 matched pairs), $244.7M total profits, 5.7yr average hold, REALSCORE 4.2. This is a deep sample, not a handful of trades — genuine evidence the project does not lose owners money.
79 years of lease remaining — no financing or decay pressure for this holding period.

Jurong Region Line opening in stages from 2026 (Corporation station ~282m); CRL CR19 in 2032; JLD buildout continuing. Narrative support, though the backtest gives future-infrastructure zero measured forward power.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Soft for this specific unit. realsmart records 72 rental contracts in the past month at $4.79 avg psf, with a 3BR median of $5,300 and the latest 12 spanning $4,700-6,800 — all against 1,000-1,300 sqft units. Tenant demand at Boon Lay is genuinely deep (NTU, Jurong industrial estate, Jurong Point retail), so the unit will let. But rent is paid for liveable, air-conditioned area, and a 3BR/2-bath configuration does not command a premium over the 3BR/3-bath mainstream stock regardless of strata size. Expect $5,000-5,500, i.e. ~3.0-3.3% gross and ~1.7-1.9% net on $1.99M — below the scorer's $6,025 / 3.63% assumption, which wrongly scales a project-wide 3BR average onto padded strata area. If the unit is ground-floor PES, aircraft and interchange noise plus the reported industrial odours will also thin the tenant pool at the top of that range.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Set the trailing 6.87% aside — it is a pooled size-mix artifact (2021-22 Centris prints skew to penthouse/PES formats at $833-977 psf; 2025-26 prints skew to mainstream 900-1,300 sqft at $1,600-1,700), the same failure mode already logged for this codebase. The honest forward anchor is the OCR realized baseline of roughly 3.7%/yr, and this unit should lag it rather than beat it: the compromised-format tier is where a mass-market project's marginal buyer disappears first, and it has no valuation gap left to close since the ask already sits at that tier's clearing level. I carry 3.5%/yr. The project as a whole is a different and better story — mainstream Centris stock has genuine MRT-integration support and a 97.7% profitable record — but that is an argument for buying a different unit here, not this one.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No profile exists for The Centris (status: not_researched), and the listing carries no floor or facing data, so the stack join is empty and the low-floor trust rules could not evaluate. Inference from URA prints is nonetheless strong. Of 108 project prints only one is exactly 1,561 sqft: Nov-21, floor 16 to 20, $1,300,000 at $833 psf — the lowest PSF in the project that year against a 2021 project median of $1,174. That size therefore belongs to a top-floor void/loft or an equivalently padded format. The last-24-month tier structure is unambiguous: floors 06-10 median $1,634 (n=15), floors 11-15 median $1,640 (n=20), floors 01-05 $1,277/$1,251/$801 (n=3), floors 16-20 $1,278/$1,175 (n=2). The subject's $1,275 psf lands on the compromised tier's median. Whether it is a ground-floor PES or a top-floor loft cannot be resolved without the floor number — but both readings give the same verdict, which is why confidence is medium rather than low. A buyer must view in person and confirm how much of the 1,561 sqft is enclosed, air-conditioned floor area versus patio or double-volume void. Recommended follow-up: run /research-development "The Centris" so the PES and penthouse stacks are profiled and this artifact is caught by the join in future scans.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: OCR realized forward baseline (+3.7%/yr, 28-district URA panel) with a small haircut for the compromised-format tier's thinner marginal buyer. Trailing ura_5yr_cagr of 6.87% rejected as a pooled size-mix artifact — 2021-22 Centris prints skew to penthouse/PES formats at $833-977 psf while 2025-26 prints skew to mainstream 900-1,300 sqft at $1,600-1,700, so the pooled series measures mix rotation, not price growth.

history.summary: A 1,561 sqft top-floor penthouse at The Centris (Boon Lay MRT lobby-to-platform, 610 units, 79yr lease) asking $2.08M / $1,332 psf, 3BR/2-bath — and, per the agent's own listing copy, 'originally a 2 bedroom apartment' partitioned into more rooms. The 829 score and 85 valuation both rest on a -11% to -12% 'discount' to the size-band median that is really the project's permanent ~-22% penthouse/PES tier level. Measured against that tier's own prints (16-20 floor: $1,175 Aug-24, $1,278 Dec-25; 01-05 floor: $1,251 Jun-25; the identical 1,561 sqft size last sold Nov-21 on floors 16-20) the ask is ~4% ABOVE the tier's best print in 24 months. The seller cut to $1.88M in August, then relisted yesterday at $2.08M — +$200k, +10.6% — the same reverse-cut pattern seen at Centro Residences. Downside record is excellent at project level (REALSCORE 4.2, 97.8% profitable on 604 matched resales) but that record was built by the 870-1,440 sqft mainstream stock, not this format.
history.rating_rationale: Avoid at $2.08M; this same listing was Neutral at $1.99M in July because that price sat at the format tier's median, and it would be Neutral again around $1.85-1.95M. Three things changed or firmed up since. (1) The format is now confirmed, not inferred: the agent's copy calls it a penthouse that was originally a 2-bedroom — so ~1,561 sqft of strata area wraps a 2BR liveable core plus roof terrace/void, which explains the 2 baths at 780 sqft/bath while every mainstream 1,227-1,572 sqft Centris listing carries 3. That is the classic strata-padding artifact the rubric says to verify before crediting any discount, and once verified the discount is gone. (2) The ask now exceeds the format's own prints: the top-floor tier cleared $1,175 psf (Aug-24, 1,744 sqft) and $1,278 psf (Dec-25, 1,744 sqft), the ground tier $1,251 (Jun-25, 1,582 sqft), and the exact 1,561 sqft size last sold on floors 16-20 in Nov-21 at $833 psf. $1,332 psf is +4% over the tier's best 24-month print and +6.5% over its median — an ask_above_own_stack_prints case that the scorer could not see because the listing carries no floor field and no stack profile exists (low_floor component 0.00). (3) Seller behaviour: $1.99M (Jul) → $1.88M (Aug 12) → $2.08M (Sep 17 relist). A $200k reversal after a cut is a seller repricing to the mainstream tier's optics, not to this unit's comps. The score's two largest components — age_value +9.38 and psf_value +4.83, ~14 of the ~51 MMR points above base — are the phantom discount; strip them and the unit is market-typical. Carry is thin: rent tracks the 2BR liveable area, not 1,561 sqft, so ~$4,800-5,300/mo → 2.8-3.1% gross, ~1.6% net on $2.08M, against the scorer's 3.48%. Exit is the real risk for an investor: in 5 years of URA prints only 18 of 108 are 1,450+ sqft and every one cleared at a 20-30% PSF discount to the mainstream stock; the JRL has slipped to 2028-29, so the one catalyst within a 5-7yr hold is no longer certain to land inside it. High confidence because the evidence is physical and documented (format, floor tier, own prints, price history), not a score gap. What would change the call: a print of this format at or above $1,332 psf, or the ask returning to ~$1.9M.
red_flags: Ask is ABOVE the format's own prints. Penthouse/16-20 floor tier: $1,175 psf (Aug-24, 1,744 sqft), $1,278 psf (Dec-25, 1,744 sqft); ground/PES tier $1,251 (Jun-25, 1,582 sqft). $1,332 psf is +4% above the best 24-month print in the tier and +6.5% above its median. The exact 1,560.78 sqft size last transacted Nov-21 on floors 16-20 at $833 psf ($1.30M).

Format confirmed: the agent's own copy describes a penthouse 'originally a 2 bedroom apartment' partitioned into more rooms (search snippet lists 4 bedrooms; feed says 3BR/2ba). 780 sqft per bathroom vs 3 baths on every mainstream 1,227-1,572 sqft Centris listing. Strata area is padded with roof terrace/void, not liveable space — the -11%/-12% 'discount' vs the size band is the project's permanent format tier, not value.

Price history is a reverse cut: $1.99M (28 Jul) → $1.88M (12 Aug) → $2.08M (17 Sep relist), +$200k / +10.6% in five weeks with no comp support. Same pattern as Centro Residences 500075630 (Avoid). Single listing id, single agent — this is not the unit-group chaining artifact.

Score artifact: age_value +9.38 and psf_value +4.83 dominate the 829 and both derive from the phantom discount; low_floor damper = 0.00 because the DB record has no floor_level and no stack profile exists, so neither the v3.8 print-contradiction rule nor the v3.12 low-floor demotion could fire. Valuation 85 and exit_demand 92.6 are contaminated the same way (exit_demand credits the mainstream stock's liquidity to this format).

Exit liquidity for this format is thin and always concessionary: 18 of 108 prints since Jun-21 are 1,450+ sqft, all cleared at $801-1,278 psf while mainstream stock cleared $1,557-1,726 in the same months. 'Deep buyer pool' and 50+ deals/yr belong to the 870-1,440 sqft units.

Weak carry: rent follows the 2BR liveable core, not 1,561 sqft. Project 3BR median ~$5,300 (realsmart, 72 contracts) is the ceiling; $4,800-5,300 → 2.8-3.1% gross, ~1.6% net on $2.08M vs scorer's 3.48% gross (rental_cache is 100 days stale, confidence already damped).

Trailing 6.87% ura_5yr_cagr is a size-mix artifact (2021-22 prints penthouse/PES-heavy at $833-999 psf; 2025-26 prints mainstream at $1,600-1,726). Same-size mainstream resale-to-resale Sep-24→May-26 is ~+2-3%/yr. Do not read the headline as forward.

Jurong Region Line has slipped: JRL1 mid-2028, JRL2 2028, JRL3 2029 (was 'from 2026' in the July eval). Corporation station at 282m may not open inside a 5-yr hold; and the backtest gives future-infra zero forward power anyway.
17 years old, in the 15-20yr segment where age-PSF decay re-accelerates to ~2.6%/yr; top-floor units carry roof-waterproofing and terrace maintenance exposure the 2-bath count does nothing to offset.

Resident-reported negatives that a roof-terrace unit takes in full: low-flying aircraft noise (Tengah flight path), industrial odours, Boon Lay bus interchange traffic noise directly below; no guest parking. JLD white site (up to 1,200 private units) is competing supply inside the exit window.
catalysts: Best-in-class connectivity: Boon Lay MRT (EW27, future JS8) 110m with integrated Jurong Point mall and bus interchange — MRT proximity is one of the few forward signals that survives clustering (std_β −0.11).
OCR region, the strongest realized forward segment in the backtest (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).

Project-level downside record is genuinely deep: REALSCORE 4.2, 97.8% profitable — 590 profitable vs 14 unprofitable on 604 matched resales, $245.4M total profits, 5.7yr avg hold, 1,189 total transactions, last print 21-Aug-2026. Read as 'this project rarely loses owners money', not as a forward rate — and note the record is built on mainstream stock.
79 years of lease remaining — no financing or decay pressure over a 5-7yr hold.
Roof-terrace penthouse format has own-stay appeal for a buyer who wants outdoor space above Jurong Point; that buyer is the exit, and pays this tier's PSF, not the tower's.

Jurong Region Line has slipped: JRL1 mid-2028, JRL2 2028, JRL3 2029 (was 'from 2026' in the July eval). Corporation station at 282m may not open inside a 5-yr hold; and the backtest gives future-infra zero forward power anyway.
17 years old, in the 15-20yr segment where age-PSF decay re-accelerates to ~2.6%/yr; top-floor units carry roof-waterproofing and terrace maintenance exposure the 2-bath count does nothing to offset.

Resident-reported negatives that a roof-terrace unit takes in full: low-flying aircraft noise (Tengah flight path), industrial odours, Boon Lay bus interchange traffic noise directly below; no guest parking. JLD white site (up to 1,200 private units) is competing supply inside the exit window.
catalysts: Best-in-class connectivity: Boon Lay MRT (EW27, future JS8) 110m with integrated Jurong Point mall and bus interchange — MRT proximity is one of the few forward signals that survives clustering (std_β −0.11).
OCR region, the strongest realized forward segment in the backtest (+3.7%/yr vs RCR +3.1%, CCR +1.9%).

Project-level downside record is genuinely deep: REALSCORE 4.2, 97.8% profitable — 590 profitable vs 14 unprofitable on 604 matched resales, $245.4M total profits, 5.7yr avg hold, 1,189 total transactions, last print 21-Aug-2026. Read as 'this project rarely loses owners money', not as a forward rate — and note the record is built on mainstream stock.
79 years of lease remaining — no financing or decay pressure over a 5-7yr hold.
Roof-terrace penthouse format has own-stay appeal for a buyer who wants outdoor space above Jurong Point; that buyer is the exit, and pays this tier's PSF, not the tower's.
agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Scorer: $6,025/mo (ura_project_bed, 62 contracts, 12mo, confidence 0.81 pre-damp; rental_cache 100 days stale) → 3.48% gross / 1.98% net. Too high for this unit: rent follows the liveable 2BR core plus a terrace premium, not 1,561 sqft of strata. realsmart's 3BR median is ~$5,300 (72 contracts, $4,700-6,800 range); a converted-2BR penthouse should be assumed at $4,800-5,300. On $2.08M that is 2.8-3.1% gross, ~1.6% net after MCST/tax/vacancy — carry-negative on any leverage above ~50% LTV. Tenant pool is families and Jurong-area corporate relocations; the terrace is a plus for some, the aircraft and interchange noise a minus.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Headline 6.87% ura_5yr_cagr (108 txns) is a size-mix artifact and must not be used. Same-size mainstream resale-to-resale: 1,238-1,302 sqft units $1,582-1,688 psf (Sep-24) → $1,642-1,695 (May-26), roughly +2-3%/yr. The penthouse tier itself: $1,175 (Aug-24) → $1,278 (Dec-25) on two 1,744 sqft prints, ~+6.5%/yr but far too thin to trust and still 25% below the tower. Forward, the right prior is the OCR region baseline (config 3.7%, realized +3.7%) applied to a fair entry — and this entry is ~4-6% above fair for the format, which consumes the first ~1.5 years of expected appreciation. Override set to 3.0% (mainstream resale-to-resale, with the format's structural discount as a drag).
